pr_title: Support all return types from handler in filters
pr_body:
This PR fixes an issue where users could not apply route handler filters to endpoints that returned void, void-returning `Task`s and `ValueTask`s, and generic `ValueTask` or `Task`.

#### Technical Detail
The current implementation of filters has logic that wraps the user provided handler into a method that complies with the `RouteHandlerFilterDelegateSignature`, namely it must return a `ValueTask<object?>` and take in a `RouteHandlerInvocationContext`. To map the return types correctly, the implementation previously indiscriminately applied `ValueTask.FromResult<object?>()` to whatever the route handler returned. This meant that you could sometimes have invocations like `ValueTask.FromResult(VoidReturningMethod())` or `ValueTask.FromResult(new Task("foo"))`.

To resolve this issue, we are improving the mapping of route handler types to `ValueTask<object?>` to account for three scenarios:

- Void returning methods
- Non-generic `Task` and `ValueTask`
- Generic `Task` and `ValueTask`

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/41213

## Customer Impact

Without this fix, customers are not able to apply route handler filters to any endpoint in their application with running into exceptions or strange behavior. This bug fix allows us to achieve the stated goal of filters being applicable on all endpoints.

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [X] No

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [X] Low

Change was validated manually and with automated tests. Surface area of change limited to user code that has handlers with the 3 return types outlined above.

## Verification

- [X] Manual (required)
- [X] Automated

## Packaging changes reviewed?

- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No
- [x] N/A

issue_context.title: Route handler filters don't handle all return types
comments: The null ref is issue https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/41188, you can workaround it by using a method instead of an inline delegate.

review_comments: Should we special case `ValueTask<object?>` and `Task<object?>` so we don't unnecessarily wrap them?

I was able to do this for `ValueTask<object?>` but the type checking on the `Expression.Condition` expects the arguments to strictly match so the `Task` has to be unwrapped and rewrapped as a `ValueTask`.
Just want to go on record saying I'm not happy with this

I'm with you. Since we're all pretty annoyed by this, I've filed https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/41330 to see if we could possibly remove the cyclic dependencies we have in our assemblies at the moment.

Sadly, this doesn't work though. I also played with `return Unsafe.As<ValueTask<T>, ValueTask<object>>(ref retval);` and while this seems to work for already-completed `ValueTask<T>` instances where `_obj` is the `T` reference type, it breaks when `_obj` is really a `Task<T>` with `EntryPointNotFoundException`s because [this](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1a181875e50e9f58be86dfca7645e4d6ccd9ec6d/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/Tasks/ValueTask.cs#L686-L691) fails to cast `_obj` to `Task<object>`, and `IValueTaskSource<object>.GetStatus(short)` doesn't exist in the vtable.
Good catch! I just pushed c1cca8b91d13d28e9ca94bbd57d690378e86c5e3 with a fix for this.
